name: Flying Attack
summary: Not truly a combat maneuver on its own, the flying attack is a modifier that may be applied to most basic attack maneuvers, at the Gamemaster's discretion.
flavor: Not truly a combat maneuver on its own, the flying attack is a modifier that may be applied to most basic attack maneuvers, at the Gamemaster's discretion. This maneuver add-on increases the momentum of the attack it is applied to by leaping and "flying" through the air to strike the target. However, using a flying attack leaves the attacker somewhat open to counterattack because they cannot change their course or easily manipulate their center of gravity until they land. A normal kick maneuver becomes a flying kick by first taking a run at the opponent, launching into the air, and then kicking while airborne, much like a specialized aerial slam attack. All modifiers associated with the flying attack are compounded (or canceled out, as the case may be) by those of the attack it is being applied to. A flying full roundhouse kick would have the following game statistics: Standard action, Damage Str +9 maximum (depending on distance run before leaping), critical on 19- 20, -2 to attack, -2 to dodge, -4 to parry, with Empowered Critical 2 (the maximum ranks allowed), Enhanced Knockback 2, and Push Over 2.

Creating New Maneuvers Eventually, you or your players will likely want to create new basic and advanced combat maneuvers. This will be especially true if you want to try your hand at making your own fighting styles. So, let's look at some guidelines and suggestions for designing new combat maneuvers. Creating new basic combat maneuvers is comparatively simple because their nature limits them to power builds that are relatively realistic. Advanced combat maneuvers, however, can include just about anything so long as it is explained away as a matter of the game's more unusual elements, such as mysticism or chi. Either way, though, the process of building the new combat maneuver is mostly the same. A good place to start when building a new combat maneuver is with the concept. You must know what you want the combat maneuver to do and how it will be portrayed in the game (that is to say, what its descriptor and function shall be). From there, figure out how to go about doing it. The following section should help you work this all out. Building with Effect Following are a variety of ideas and suggestions on how some effects may be used to create new advanced (and yes, even basic) combat maneuvers. Generally speaking, Gamemasters should limit the introduction of new combat maneuvers for an existing style to masters (or even Grandmasters, as per the Benefit advantage). summary: You can build up a devastating consequence for a series of successful attacks.
flavor: You can build up a devastating consequence for a series of successful attacks. You are afforded (rank x 5) points to purchase a Combo Finish effect. A Combo Finish may only be used if you have gained some Combo Points (see the Combo Element extra, pg 91, and advantage, pg 59) equal to twice your Combo Finish ranks. Your Combo Finish power may be unleashed on the first available standard action once you have met the Combo Point requirements. You may possess different Combo Finish powers with different costs--you decide which one to unleash if you have the necessary Combo Points for more than one. Any remaining Combo Points after you use a Combo Finish are lost. This Combo Finish attack must be a single power build with one or multiple effects but cannot contain separate powers or an array. It cannot purchase ranks in another Combo Finish, a device, Extra Attacks, Summon, power effect with the Area extra (although some Gamemasters may allow the latter in more cinematic or super-hero oriented games), or any other power the Gamemaster determines is inappropriate for a Combo Finish attack. Also, a Combo Finish must be its own power, and cannot be a component in another power build or part of an array. A Combo Finish effect must include at least one power effect that involves an opposed check, attack, or the target making a resistance check--it must impose some form of effect on the target. Combo Actions A character gains Combo Points by successfully using a power with the Combo Element extra (pg 91) or advantage (pg 59. Employing such a trait is known as using a Combo Action. A Combo Action always has a particular target and involves a resistance check or opposed roll. The Combo Action is considered successful for the purpose of gaining Combo Points if the target is struck and must make a Toughness, Fortitude, or Will resistance check (respectively) in response. This is regardless of whether the resistance check succeeds or not. Accumulating Combo Points A character gains one Combo Point if a single degree of success is obtained with a Combo Action, whether the Combo Actions are made against the same or different targets. Double the Combo Points per degree of success after the first (i.e., two points for two degrees of success, four points for three degrees, eight points for four degrees, etc.) You can continue to increase your accumulated Combo Points by completing Combo Actions in successive, unbroken rounds. A character loses all their accumulated Combo Points if, by the end of the current round, they have not succeeded at a Combo Action. Retaining Combo Points If, for some reason, you need to hold your accumulated Combo Points until a better opportunity to use them presents itself, you may attempt to do so. As a free action, you can keep your accumulated Combo Points without further accumulation for a round with a successful (DC 10 +1 for every consecutive round) Will resistance check. You can only attempt the resistance check if you have obtained enough Combo Points to unleash at least one of your Combo Finish powers. Otherwise, you must continue accumulating points or risk losing them, as normal. Chapter 4: Powers Alternatively, the character can spend a hero point at any moment during the round to retain accumulated Combo Points that should be lost due to an inability to complete a successful Combo Action. Doing so allows them a single round to perform non-Combo Actions or make up for failed Combo Actions.

Ammunition +0 or +1 cost per rank The power effect to which this extra is applied is meant to represent a special form of ammunition that cannot be effectively used on its own. You must indicate the specific type of weapon (e.g., bow, crossbow, heavy pistol) the ammunition operates in. This extra prevents power effects of radically different ranks from resulting in equally disparate ranges that don't conceptually make sense. If the ammunition is intended to have a different range from that of the device that uses it, such as with a rocket-propelled crossbow bolt, don't apply this extra.
